scholarships.title: EASL Mobility / Research Fellowship Programme
scholarships.official_source: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)

eligibility: Early- or mid-career professional in hepatology research or clinical practice
Affiliated with a recognised clinical / scientific institution or university in Europe
Host institute must be based in Europe (mobility fellowships)
Research or project focus must be on liver disease
Strong motivation for a career in clinical or basic hepatology research (research fellowships)
Letter from the host institute confirming the ability to host the applicant (mobility fellowships)
existing.eligibility_summary: Early- or mid-career professionals affiliated with a recognised clinical or scientific institution or university in Europe, must be EASL members, and the project must focus on liver disease. Mobility fellowships additionally require a host institute in Europe and a letter confirming it can host the applicant.
benefits: Laboratory supplies, equipment and research-related expenses
Other logistical costs needed to execute the fellowship, including childcare
coverage: Laboratory supplies, equipment and research-related expenses
Other logistical costs needed to execute the fellowship, including childcare
requirements: Active EASL membership to access the Memberzone application portal
Research or project proposal of a maximum of 5 pages
Curriculum vitae of a maximum of 4 pages
Recommendation letter from a supervisor or mentor, maximum 1 page
documents: Supervisor or mentor recommendation letter (max. 1 page)
Host institute letter confirming ability to host (mobility fellowships only)
application_method: Submit the application through the EASL Memberzone portal; an active EASL membership is required
existing.selection_notes: Applications are scored out of 100 by an expert review panel appointed by the EASL Governing Board, with funding awarded to the highest overall scores. Weighting published by EASL: scientific/clinical merit 35%, applicant's motivation 20%, applicant's potential 15%, relevance to hepatology 15%, host institution and environment 15%. Final decisions also consider diversity, equity and potential long-term impact.
existing.best_fit: Early- to mid-career hepatology researchers and clinicians based at a European institution who want a six-month research placement abroad or a funded project at their current host.
existing.notes: Preference may be given to applicants from Inclusiveness Target Countries for mobility fellowships. Award notifications for the 2026 round were scheduled for November 2026.
existing.program_type: Professional association research and mobility fellowship
